**Illegality cannot be determined from this evidence alone.** The data indicate 13.5 hectares of tree-cover loss in 2025, of which 13.1 hectares overlap areas mapped as native forest by Uruguay’s MGAP in 2021. However, no later year is available to corroborate the event under the tool’s stated rule.

The evidence does not establish why the trees were lost or whether any required authorization was granted. A legal assessment would require checking the cause and extent of the clearing, applicable Uruguayan law, and relevant permits or exemptions with the competent authorities.
